To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of hydrated quicklime with extended mellowing, to produce high strength clay clods, can cause the development of inter clod pores.
the durability of a lime treated soil is strongly influenced by: 1. The degree of inter-clod porosity 2. The degree of sulphate present in the soil 3. The temperature of the curing
the use of hydrated (slaked) lime, with the addition of water throughout mellowing and mixing periods is the best way to minimise the risk of sulphate swell failure in lime stabilised clay soils.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding of lime stabilised materials and the practical implications of this understanding for field applications.
the fundamental understanding of the chemical reactions that occur during the lime stabilisation process, and how these reactions are influenced by the preparation method.
understanding the mechanisms of lime stabilisation, with a view to improving the durability and performance of the material in the ground.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
lime stabilisation of cohesive soils can provide durable ground improvement when the working method is adapted to minimise inter clod porosities and the ingress of sulphate bearing water.
the use of quick lime with short mellowing periods is not suitable for the treatment of high sulphate soils.
the sulphate content of the clay fill material should not be the sole consideration in the selection and design of the lime stabilisation treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of hydrated lime to clay soils, in a field relevant way, results in a material with a high potential durability.
the use of quick lime with long mellowing periods and dry of optimum compaction should be avoided.
the use of hydrated line with extended mellowing times, and the addition of GGBS can be used to improve the durability of clay fills to sulphate attack.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lime stabilised clay soils can have very high strength, however, the durability to water ingress is dependent on the method of treatment and the degree of post compaction porosity.
the long term durability is improved when the lime is distributed throughout the soil and not just on the surface of the clods.
